title: The hundred and one years
hook: Indra's last lesson after 101 years: the fourth, the awareness every state appears in
carry: turiya: the awareness under every state
tomorrow: The student who asked about om

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Mandukya Upanishad: prajna, deep sleep, a mass of knowing, made of bliss. And Indra walked back a third time.

Prajapati told Indra: stay five more years. Thirty-two, thirty-two, thirty-two, five. One hundred and one years, the story says, Indra lived as a student, and he was the king of the gods. Then came the last teaching. This body is mortal, held by death. But it's the home of a self that has no body and doesn't die. The one who knows 'let me hear this' is the self; the ear is only for hearing. The one who knows 'let me think this' is the self; the mind is its divine eye.
screen: `101 YEARS A STUDENT.` → `THE BODY: A HOME.` → `THE ONE WHO KNOWS.`

segments.voice: Not the body, not the dreamer, not the sleeper. The knower behind all of them. The Mandukya's seventh verse names the same thing, almost entirely by what it isn't. Not knowing inward: that was dream. Not knowing outward: that was waking. Not a mass of knowing: that was deep sleep. Unseen. Ungraspable. Unthinkable. Unnameable. In it the world comes to rest. Peaceful, shanta. Auspicious, shiva. Not two, advaita. This, they consider the fourth. That is the self. The verse's own word is plain, caturtha, fourth; later tradition calls it turiya. And it isn't a fourth state, a place you travel to after sleep. Here's an image modern teachers use. Three films play on one screen: a busy city, a wild dream, a long black frame. The screen isn't any of them. It's what all three play on, and it never changes. On this reading, the fourth is the awareness that waking, dream and sleep come and go in, here right now under this moment. That's the heart of Shankara's school, Advaita Vedanta. Other Hindu schools read the verse as the Lord's own nature beyond the three states. Both agree you are more than any state you pass through. Today, a life has many films on its screen: the student, the daughter, the profile, the mood of the week. Each one feels like all of you while it plays. The fourth is the Hindu answer to who's watching. It took a king of the gods a hundred and one years. You get to hear it in five minutes, and spend a lifetime on it.
screen: `NOT INWARD, NOT OUTWARD.` · `PEACEFUL, AUSPICIOUS, NOT TWO.` · `THREE FILMS, ONE SCREEN.` · `NOT A STATE: WHAT STATES APPEAR IN.` · then, large: `TURIYA.`

segments.voice: Notice that you're awake, then notice the awareness that knows you're awake; the Mandukya's map says the same awareness was there in last night's dreams, and in the deep sleep after them. Rest in that awareness itself, not in anything it's aware of. When a thought or sound arrives, let it play on the screen, and stay with the screen.
The Mandukya Upanishad. Its seventh verse: the fourth, peaceful, auspicious, not two. Not another state, but what all three appear in.
Your line: turiya, the awareness under every state. The films keep changing; the screen stays. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Mandukya verse 7 is central to Advaita Vedanta, where 'the fourth' (turiya) names pure awareness; other Vedanta schools read the verse as describing the Lord beyond the three states.

fork.reveal: the Mandukya uses a string of nots, then: peaceful, auspicious, not two. that is the self.

original.note: Sanskrit: turiya, the fourth; the later name for Mandukya 7's caturtha.

chat.meaning: Prajapati's last teaching: the self is the knower behind ear, eye and mind. The Mandukya calls it the fourth: what waking, dream and sleep appear in.

tie.story: After a hundred and one years, Prajapati taught Indra that the self is the knower behind the body, the dream and the sleep.
